title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models—uh oh, Jensen!
slides: Why are banned Nvidia chips powering China's top AI?
Export rules were meant to stop exactly this
The chips arrived before the ban, stockpiled quietly
Some firms may face audits on chip provenance
Check your supply chain before regulators do
thread_text:
1. Banned chips, top AI

Nvidia's restricted GPUs are still running China's most advanced AI models. The export controls didn't stop the compute—they just made it invisible.

2. The loophole was timing

Most of those chips entered China legally before the bans took effect. Firms stockpiled quietly, and by the time rules changed, the hardware was already racked.

3. Now regulators want receipts

Audits are coming for companies that can't prove where their chips came from. Provenance documentation is becoming the new compliance battleground.

4. Supply chain blind spots

Many firms don't know which generation of chips sits in their own racks. That ignorance is now a legal liability, not just an operational gap.

5. Audit yourself first

Pull your hardware inventory today and trace every GPU back to its import date. If you can't, regulators will do it for you.

instagram.caption:
The most advanced AI models coming out of China right now are running on Nvidia chips that the US banned from export. 🧐

Most of those GPUs entered the country legally before the rules took effect — firms quietly stockpiled them, and by the time the bans landed, the hardware was already racked and running.

Now regulators are demanding proof of where those chips came from, and companies that can't trace their provenance are facing audits.

If you work with AI infrastructure, pull your hardware inventory and trace every GPU back to its import date. 📋

Can you actually prove where your chips came from — or would an audit catch you off guard? 🤔
